newsitem.title: GUYANA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR, DRAVID HIT 50S ON SLOW DAY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR, DRAVID HIT 50S ON SLOW DAY.

text.p: Captain Sachin Tendulkar and Rahul Dravid made half-centuries to frustrate the West Indies bowlers as the fifth and final test got off to a slow start on Thursday.

India, who made just 38 runs in the opening session, reached 194 for two at the close with Tendulkar not out 62 and Dravid unbeaten on 71, the pair so far featuring in a third-wicket stand of 126 runs.
Fortune has favoured Tendulkar and Dravid, with both offering catches which the West Indies fielders failed to take advantage of.

Fast bowler Curtly Ambrose dropped a return chance offered by Tendulkar on 11 while wicket-keeper Courtney Browne and first slip Brian Lara allowed an edged shot by Dravid off Franklyn Rose to slip between them.
Earlier, India were made to toil for runs by Curtly Ambrose and his fellow fast bowlers.
Ambrose shackled the touring team with an opening spell of 9-8-1-0 after they won the toss, and a wicket apiece for Ian Bishop and captain Courtney Walsh also kept them in check.
Bishop struck the first blow for West Indies, who lead the series 1-0 after their 38-run win in the third test, with the total 32.
Opener Ajay Jadeja got a thin edge and was caught by wicketkeeper Courtney Browne, having made eight in 98 minutes.

Jadeja's first-wicket partner, Navjot Sidhu, fell to Walsh, the most threatening of the fast bowlers, with the total 68. He had made 36 from 104 deliveries when he tried to cut and was caught by Carl Hooper at second slip.
Tendulkar's arrival brought some life to the innings and the right-hander began by hitting Walsh for four with an on-drive for four off the first ball he faced.
West Indies were unchanged from the rain-ruined drawn fourth test in Antigua, while India brought back Sidhu for Vangipurappu Laxman and fast bowler Dodda Ganesh replaced batsman Saurav Ganguly.
Rawl Lewis, the Grenada leg-spin bowler, was forced to field for the entire day, because batsman Roland Holder was struck in the face practising slip catching before the start.
Walsh twisted his left ankle in the middle of his 17th over and had to leave the field.
